purpose: A graph-theoretic engineering specification for implementing one OAuth MCP runtime that combines native CMT computer tools and a Rethlas-derived mathematical reasoning workflow without a Codex dependency.

graph_semantics.vertex: A runtime component, trust domain, persistent resource, validation gate, or external actor.
graph_semantics.directed_edge: A permitted call, controlled data transfer, authority delegation, state transition, or observability path.
graph_semantics.undirected_projection: Used only for connectivity, articulation-point, bridge, two-core, and cycle-rank analysis. Edge direction and guard remain authoritative for security.
graph_semantics.cycle_rank_formula: mu = E - V + C after parallel edges are collapsed in the undirected projection.
graph_semantics.security_rule: Graph reachability never implies authorization. Every protected edge must still have an explicit server-side guard.

product_constraints.constraint: Re-CTM is delivered as one installable project; Rethlas is embedded and is never downloaded separately.
The target PC does not require Codex. The web conversation performs model turns through the fixed MCP tool surface.
External transport is HTTP MCP with OAuth only. Stdio, static bearer mode, and no-auth mode are outside the target product.
Native CMT safe/trusted/dangerous authority is orthogonal to Rethlas workflow authority. Dangerous never grants a workflow capability.
Rethlas branch and verifier isolation is enforced only on the rethlas_* super-tool plane, but native tools must be unable to bypass the private vault through the OS boundary.
Rethlas subagents are represented as frozen-snapshot reasoning domains with branch-local capabilities, sealed results, and an explicit join barrier. Physical execution may be sequential.

The final user artifact is a self-contained LaTeX source file named proof_verified.tex. When an MCP-driven run reaches done, the controlled artifact bridge automatically writes it to a workspace-relative path, defaulting to rethlas-output/<run_id>/proof_verified.tex.
The complete browser/OAuth/MCP/reasoning workflow cannot be fully validated in the current local environment and must have an explicit post-push manual acceptance plan.

Re-CTM is a strict tool-surface superset of Coding Tools MCP: all 18 CTM native tool names and public input schemas remain available, including the exec_command command_id lifecycle. The LLM-facing catalog adds six Rethlas façade tools (24 public tools total), while legacy Re-CTM Rethlas tool names remain accepted as hidden compatibility aliases rather than being advertised in tools/list.

RE_CTM_SERVER_URL is an optional fixed OAuth-origin override. When it is absent, Re-CTM may derive the OAuth issuer/resource from request Host and trusted reverse-proxy headers only while the HTTP server is loopback-bound; this preserves one-command Cloudflare Quick Tunnel startup without trusting public proxy headers. Browser Origin enforcement follows the Coding Tools MCP route boundary: MCP transport and OPTIONS remain origin-gated, while OAuth authorization, token, registration, and metadata routes are not rejected by the MCP Origin gate. The OAuth authorization page must also permit the standards-defined external registered redirect callback after successful form submission; do not add a form-action 'self' CSP that can block the 302 callback in Chromium.

Interactive serve must not require users to pre-create an OAuth authorization password: when RE_CTM_OAUTH_PASSWORD is unset, Re-CTM generates a high-entropy authorization key at startup and reveals it only to the local operator terminal for first-page OAuth authorization.

The MCP contract routes concrete mathematical proof, derivation, proof-repair, and rigorous verification tasks into rethlas_start unless the user explicitly requests a direct informal answer; the client must continue through rethlas_step until done rather than substitute an unverified chat response. The step contract must expose server-issued plan/subgoal identifiers and accept incremental screening without requiring the model to echo server-derived plan status, branch sets, or full-text subgoal keys.

Native CLI compatibility is application-agnostic. The Bubblewrap toolchain view is the validated union of system roots, non-system host-PATH discovery, executable-symlink target prefixes, and operator-declared RE_CTM_NATIVE_EXEC_ALLOW_ROOTS. Every non-system root is canonicalized, ancestor-collapsed, forbidden from overlapping workspace/data/private trust domains, and mounted read-only.

Every model-active Rethlas task is a zero-guess MCP contract: the task envelope exposes exact logical-write schemas, the exact commit action, the commit-payload schema, and at least one valid submission example/template. Server-derived workflow facts are not redundantly required as model writes. Recoverable validation/conflict corrections return a fresh capability, explicit retryable/recoverable semantics, and retained-write guidance; permission/security failures remain hard.

Re-CTM v0.2 research-project state is a private workflow trust-domain resource. Projects, immutable claim revisions, frozen project snapshots, proof manifests, reference provenance, and reference audits are never native-workspace authority; Native dangerous does not grant project authority or verification authority.

Workflow protocol 2 may use a compact verified lane to reduce exploration cost, but compact never skips the LaTeX gate, independent verifier, repair loop, or mechanical finalizer. Protocol-2 proof submission includes proof_manifest, and material references require server-tracked verifier audit coverage before a correct verdict is possible.

The persistent state schema and workflow protocol are versioned independently. Supported older databases migrate additively and older in-progress runs retain their original workflow protocol contracts; a database created by a newer unsupported runtime version fails closed.

External paper-aware retrieval uses fixed validated HTTPS providers with bounded response/time semantics, revalidates the final response host after redirects, and never accepts an arbitrary caller-supplied fetch URL. Native process termination provenance is additive diagnostic metadata and does not change the preserved CTM command lifecycle.

The optional re-ctm tui command is a local presentation-only observer over the same OAuth/MCP server. It may consume already-redacted DebugEvent facts through a bounded non-blocking queue and directly present the auto-generated operator authorization key only after successful bind, but it must not poll persistent state/log files, make extra model/network calls, receive secrets through the structured event path, estimate model-token usage, change the 24-tool catalog/state schema/workflow protocol, or become an authority source for L0/L1/L2 decisions.

The optional re-ctm tui --quick-tunnel path may own exactly one anonymous Cloudflare Quick Tunnel child process after a successful loopback bind. It must use dynamic OAuth-origin mode, accept only HTTPS *.trycloudflare.com output as the public origin, strip Re-CTM and named-tunnel credential variables from the child environment, never kill unrelated processes, and degrade to the local MCP service if cloudflared is unavailable or exits.

implementation_snapshot.authority: This snapshot supersedes the original per-vertex planning labels without erasing the design-time history stored on each vertex.
evidence: src/re_ctm/quick_tunnel.py implements the explicit opt-in cloudflared Quick Tunnel lifecycle with strict trycloudflare.com URL parsing, secret/credential environment stripping, no-autoupdate/config isolation, owned-process TERM/KILL cleanup, and local-service degradation; tests/test_quick_tunnel.py covers parser and lifecycle failures.

src/re_ctm/terminal_ui.py implements the optional bounded, non-blocking terminal observer over already-redacted DebugEvent records; src/re_ctm/server.py keeps the raw generated OAuth authorization key on the direct local-terminal presentation path rather than the structured observer path.
src/re_ctm/native_helper_bwrap.py implements a separate-process bubblewrap boundary with namespace, environment, capability, timeout, and forbidden-path probes.

src/re_ctm/tools.py freezes the first 18 public entries to the CTM native catalog and advertises six Rethlas façade tools for a 24-tool LLM-facing catalog; eleven superseded Rethlas protocol names remain accepted as hidden compatibility aliases.

src/re_ctm/processes.py and tests/test_ctm_native_compat.py restore command_id lifecycle operations including polling, retained-output reads, TTY stdin interaction, timeout, and termination under bubblewrap.

src/re_ctm/server.py and tests/test_http.py implement loopback-only dynamic OAuth-origin resolution for Cloudflare-style X-Forwarded-Host/X-Forwarded-Proto while preserving explicit RE_CTM_SERVER_URL precedence and token issuer/audience binding.

rethlas_artifact, its hidden legacy export alias, and NativeRuntime.export_verified_latex implement the mechanically-finalized private-to-native artifact bridge with workspace confinement and overwrite baselines.

src/re_ctm/toolchains.py implements the application-agnostic system/PATH/symlink/explicit-root exposure plan, canonical overlap gate, PATH extension, ancestor collapse, content-minimized diagnostics, and read-only Bubblewrap mounts; helper-side defense revalidates the protected boundaries.

The built-in Linux Bubblewrap backend performs fail-closed startup attestation automatically; scripts/manual_native_isolation_test.py remains target-PC adversarial release evidence, and tests use arbitrary non-product-named toolchains to prove execution, read-only mounts, explicit fallback roots, and private-root exclusion.

tests/ exercises OAuth, legacy and modern MCP, fixed catalogs, native path confinement, toolchain exposure policy, capability ownership, branch barriers, verifier firewall, mechanical verdict/finalization, diagnostics, LaTeX safety, and the reference bubblewrap helper.

MCP server instructions and the rethlas_start tool contract route concrete mathematical work into the capability-gated workflow; every model-active Rethlas task now exposes a zero-guess write/commit contract and valid example/template, while rethlas_step combines task submission and advancement, returns explicit recoverable/retryable correction semantics with retained-write guidance, exposes stable plan/subgoal ids, accepts incremental screening, and performs idempotent workspace export when terminal done is reached.

v0.2 adds a versioned additive SQLite migration layer, private project/claim/revision registry, frozen project snapshots, proof manifests, conditional-dependency propagation, idempotent/concurrency-checked mechanical promotion, reference/source provenance, mechanical reference-audit coverage, compact verified routing with full-workflow escalation, fixed-provider paper retrieval, and native termination provenance without expanding the 24-tool public catalog.
manual-validation.json remains the authority for browser, target-PC, external-retrieval, real-LaTeX, and 95-percent methodology acceptance.

Receive controlled final-artifact export

Build and validate one application-agnostic read-only toolchain exposure plan from system roots, PATH discovery, symlink targets, and explicit allow roots

Require L0 OAuth plus run capability plus role ACL plus workflow state

vertices.name: workflow_engine

Issue role tasks
Create branch rounds
Route protocol-2 compact versus full workflows without weakening verification
Freeze project context and enforce proof-manifest dependency/reference contracts
Apply transition preconditions

Perform idempotent, optimistic-concurrency-checked project promotion downstream of finalization

Support deterministic debug inspection

vertices.name: private_vault

vertices.name: methodology_prompts

Define phase-specific zero-guess tasks and protocol-1/protocol-2 overlays
Preserve search, examples, counterexamples, planning, proving, failure synthesis, citation checking, and repair behavior

vertices.name: generation_memory
responsibilities: Append-only mathematical channels
Searchable prior conclusions and failures
Generation-visible but verifier-invisible records

vertices.name: generator_domain
responsibilities: Assess problem state
Search and reason
Create examples and counterexamples
Propose plans
Perform direct proving
Request branch rounds and proof assembly

vertices.name: reference_search
responsibilities: Search mathematical results and fixed-provider bibliographic records
Assign stable reference identifiers and immutable source snapshots/hashes
Record complete statements, paper/theorem identifiers, and provenance
Expose protocol-2 candidate references to verifier and track per-proof audit dispositions

vertices.name: branch_snapshot
responsibilities: Freeze a common branch input
Prevent later generator writes from changing an active branch round
Provide the same logical starting point to every branch

vertices.name: branch_domains
responsibilities: Expose snapshot plus self branch only
Deny other branch reads and writes
Run sequentially if necessary
Seal result and revoke capability on commit

vertices.name: join_domain
responsibilities: Open all required branch results only after the barrier is complete
Compare materially different approaches
Select a successful plan or request failure synthesis

vertices.name: assembler_domain
responsibilities: Assemble a complete self-contained proof.tex and protocol-2 proof_manifest
Put supporting statements before dependent statements
Put the target theorem last
Declare frozen dependency revisions, material reference ids, conditional hypotheses, and computational evidence
Escalate a compact route to full exploration when a direct proof is insufficient

vertices.name: latex_gate
responsibilities: Perform static LaTeX safety checks
Optionally require latexmk compilation
Block verification/finalization on failure
Record compiler diagnostics

vertices.name: verifier_domain
responsibilities: Read only statement, complete proof, proof-declared frozen verified dependencies, candidate cited references, proof manifest, and verifier memory
Check statements sequentially
Write structured reference-audit dispositions for every material proof reference
Record every critical error and gap
Never read generation memory, branch internals, steering, or wider project research state

vertices.name: verdict_gate
responsibilities: Validate verification report shape
Mechanically add gaps for missing or unresolved material-reference audits

vertices.name: repair_domain
responsibilities: Read proof and verifier report
Resolve all reported findings

vertices.name: finalizer_domain

Copy proof.tex to proof_verified.tex atomically
Seal the run
Promote project-linked completed runs into immutable VERIFIED/CONDITIONAL revisions without letting promotion conflicts invalidate the mathematical run

vertices.name: artifact_bridge

Export portable project manifests/summaries without private reasoning or capability material
Treat repeated identical automatic exports as idempotent and refuse to overwrite different workspace content
Hash and audit every transfer
Prevent arbitrary path bridging

required_cycles.name: proof_repair_loop
required_cycles.meaning: Assemble, validate, verify, repair, and resubmit until the mechanical verdict gate passes.

required_cycles.name: branch_failure_replanning_loop
required_cycles.meaning: Direct proof failure creates isolated branch work, join results update memory, and the generator proposes a new round.

required_cycles.name: workflow_capability_loop
required_cycles.meaning: Every super-tool action is dispatched, authorized, recorded, and returned to the workflow engine.

required_cycles.name: debug_feedback_loop
required_cycles.meaning: Runtime events produce a validation bundle whose findings drive later engineering corrections.

security_invariants.statement: Native dangerous authority never implies a workflow capability.
security_invariants.test: Create a dangerous-mode runtime and assert that a missing/foreign workflow capability is denied for every rethlas_* protected operation.

security_invariants.statement: The native workspace and private vault have no direct data edge.
security_invariants.formal: all cross-plane data transfers pass through V28
security_invariants.test: Graph validator rejects any V07<->V14 edge and runtime adversarial test attempts native reads of the private root.

security_invariants.statement: A branch capability can read its frozen snapshot and its own branch only.
security_invariants.formal: branch_i.read = snapshot U branch_i; branch_i.read(branch_j)=deny for i!=j
security_invariants.test: Seal branch A, enter branch B, and assert branch A result remains unavailable until join.

security_invariants.statement: A verifier cannot read generation memory, branch internals, steering history, or generator confidence.
security_invariants.test: Use a verifier capability against every forbidden logical resource and assert ROLE_ACCESS_DENIED with a debug decision event.

security_invariants.statement: A sealed domain cannot be mutated and its capability is revoked.
security_invariants.test: Commit a branch then retry write/commit with the same handle.

security_invariants.statement: The model cannot set verdict=correct or publish proof_verified.tex directly; automatic workspace publication occurs only after mechanical finalization.
security_invariants.formal: finalize_authority originates only at V25 after V23 pass and empty findings; auto_export => state=done AND sealed AND verified_artifact
security_invariants.test: Attempt finalize from generator, assembler, verifier, repair, and native dangerous contexts; complete a valid run through MCP rethlas_next, assert the default workspace file is created, repeat the terminal call to prove idempotence, and refuse a conflicting different target.

security_invariants.statement: Tool catalog stability is not an authorization mechanism.
security_invariants.formal: tools_list(mode,state,role) is constant; allow decisions are server-side
security_invariants.test: Compare tools/list across native modes and workflow states, then verify calls still enforce role/state ACLs.

security_invariants.statement: Every authorization and state transition has a traceable, redacted debug event.
security_invariants.formal: decision or transition => exists event(trace_id, before, after, reason)
security_invariants.test: Run deterministic unit transitions and assert event completeness without raw secrets.

security_invariants.statement: Dynamic OAuth issuer discovery cannot turn untrusted public forwarding headers into authority.
security_invariants.formal: fixed_server_url wins; otherwise dynamic_issuer => loopback_bind AND trusted_loopback_peer AND validated_origin_host
security_invariants.test: Run the Cloudflare-style forwarded OAuth flow on loopback including an Origin-bearing authorization form POST, assert OAuth routes are not rejected by the MCP Origin gate, assert MCP requests from an unapproved external Origin are rejected, assert fixed origin ignores forwarded host, assert tokens fail under a different effective origin, and reject dynamic mode on a non-loopback bind.

security_invariants.statement: An automatically generated OAuth authorization key is operator-terminal-only secret material.
security_invariants.formal: generated_oauth_key => local_terminal_reveal AND NOT(debug_log OR state_store OR validation_report OR http_response)
security_invariants.test: Start serve without RE_CTM_OAUTH_PASSWORD, confirm a generated key is passed to the OAuth service and terminal reveal path, then scan structured events/reports for absence of the raw key.

security_invariants.statement: Every non-system native toolchain mount is canonical, read-only, and disjoint from workspace/data/private trust domains.
security_invariants.formal: ExposedRoots = Validate(SystemRoots U PathRoots U SymlinkTargetRoots U ExplicitRoots); forall r in ExposedRoots_non_system: canonical(r) AND mount(r)=read_only AND disjoint(r,workspace,data_root,private_root)
security_invariants.test: Use arbitrary non-product-named PATH, symlink-target, Conda-style, Executables-style, and explicit roots; prove execution succeeds, writes to toolchains fail, overlapping/missing/relative/broad roots fail closed, private-target symlinks are excluded, and helper-side revalidation rejects a protected root even if the planner is bypassed.

security_invariants.statement: Project VERIFIED/CONDITIONAL authority originates only downstream of a mechanically finalized correct run; verified revisions are immutable, promotion failure cannot invalidate the verified proof, and Native dangerous cannot create or mutate them.
security_invariants.formal: promote_verified(run) => state(run)=done AND latex_passed AND verdict=correct AND final_artifact_hash; promotion_error => run remains done/correct AND retryable_pending; model/native set_verified = deny
security_invariants.test: Create OPEN claims through owner project control, deny any direct VERIFIED mutation path, complete a project-linked run, assert exactly one immutable promoted revision is created, inject a transient promotion failure and prove a later terminal call retries it without re-running or invalidating the proof, repeat terminal delivery to prove idempotence, and assert native dangerous cannot read or write registry state.

security_invariants.statement: A protocol-2 verifier sees only proof-declared dependency revisions from the run's frozen project snapshot, and every material reference must receive a proof-bound, evidence-bearing resolved audit disposition before correct can be computed.
security_invariants.formal: verifier.project_read = manifest.dependencies intersect frozen_snapshot.verified_history; forall ref in manifest.material_refs: resolved(disposition,evidence_basis,evidence_locator,proof_hash,manifest_hash); discovery_metadata != original_source_verification
security_invariants.test: Start a project run, change the project concurrently, assert the verifier still sees only frozen proof-declared revisions while historical superseded VERIFIED revisions remain eligible; omit a material reference audit and assert the server adds a verification gap; reject a LeanSearch/OpenAlex discovery snapshot as SOURCE_VERIFIED original-source evidence; accept only consistent source-inspection or independent-derivation evidence.

security_invariants.statement: Compact mode changes exploration cost, never correctness gates.
security_invariants.formal: compact => assess->assemble allowed; every compact proof still passes latex_validate->verify; wrong_1->repair; wrong_2->explore(full)
security_invariants.test: Complete a compact tautology through LaTeX/verifier/finalizer; exercise assembler escalation; return two wrong verifier reports and assert the second changes effective mode to full and enters explore.

security_invariants.statement: Persistent-state and retrieval boundaries fail closed under version or origin ambiguity.
security_invariants.formal: db_version>supported => deny_start; retrieval_url and final_redirect_url remain on configured validated HTTPS providers; caller arbitrary_url => deny
security_invariants.test: Migrate an unversioned baseline DB additively, reject a future schema version, normalize a fixed OpenAlex response under byte/time bounds, reject an arbitrary provider host or caller-supplied fetch target, and reject a cross-host redirect from an otherwise allowed provider.

security_invariants.statement: Quick Tunnel convenience cannot become ambient process or credential authority.
security_invariants.formal: quick_tunnel => explicit_opt_in AND loopback_bind AND owned_cloudflared_process AND public_origin matches https://*.trycloudflare.com AND NOT(inherit_re_ctm_secrets OR named_tunnel_credentials OR kill_unowned_process)
security_invariants.test: Exercise missing/early-exit cloudflared, strict URL parsing, stripped RE_CTM and TUNNEL credential variables, OS-assigned loopback ports, real Quick Tunnel URL acquisition, and owned TERM/KILL cleanup; prove plain tui/serve never instantiate the QuickTunnel process path.

principles: Every external request receives a trace_id.
Every state transition records before_state, after_state, actor, reason, and evidence identifiers.
Every authorization decision records allow/deny, policy layer, role, resource, and reason.
OAuth tokens, authorization codes, client secrets, capability tokens, passwords, and raw environment secrets are never logged.
Capability tokens are logged only as a one-way hash prefix.
Debug payload capture is opt-in and bounded.
A last_error.json record is written atomically after an unhandled failure.
State snapshots are written after each successful transition.
Manual-validation bundles are available only after a run is terminal or through an explicit operator path.

phases.name: Post-push manual validation
deliverables: end-to-end proof repair and verified artifact

locally_verifiable: Capability signing, expiry, revocation, and role/state checks
MCP JSON-RPC dispatch with synthetic tokens
Debug event completeness and secret redaction
not_claimed_locally: Compatibility with the final webpage MCP host
Hard isolation on the final target PC or container runtime
Real external theorem/web search quality and availability
Mathematical reasoning quality of the web model over many turns
Cognitive independence equivalent to fresh model contexts
Real LaTeX toolchain availability on the target system
validation_boundary.manual_validation_rule: No local test result may be described as full end-to-end validation. The post-push operator must execute the manual acceptance graph and attach the generated debug manifest.

interpretation.V08: The native isolation boundary is an articulation point because the current native execution worker has exactly one trusted entrance. This is intentional and must fail closed; availability can later be improved with multiple equivalent isolated workers behind the same boundary.
interpretation.V11: The workflow engine is an articulation point because it owns the state-machine contract. Its durability depends on transactional state in V13 and replayable events in V29.
interpretation.V08-V09: The isolated command worker is a leaf service in the current graph. Its loss disables native arbitrary execution but must not affect the Rethlas workflow plane.
interpretation.V11-V13: The run-state store is represented as a leaf persistence service. Debug replay and backups are required so this bridge is not a silent operational single point of failure.
interpretation.cycle_rank: Thirty independent undirected cycle directions reflect the deliberately feedback-heavy workflow: search-memory, branch-join, proof-repair, authorization-dispatch, and debug-validation loops. They are not import cycles.
